description: Empirical Hack-law scaling targets from exorheic HydroRIVERS v1.0 source-to-sink backbone reaches. DBF records are streamed from the global archive; NEXT_DOWN=0, ENDORHEIC=0, ORD_CLAS=1 reaches with at least 1,000,000 km2 upstream area are fitted. Generated comparisons independently select ocean-outlet, explicitly non-endorheic watershed backbones over the same area floor.

sources.tolerance_basis: Absolute coarse-network Hack-exponent model-fit tolerance. Generated observations are restricted to explicit ocean-outlet, non-endorheic watershed backbones over the shared catchment-area floor; coarse grid resolution remains a model-fit limitation and this is not a statistical confidence interval.

sources.source_citation: Lehner, B. and Grill, G. (2013). Global river hydrography and network routing: baseline data and new approaches to study the world's large river systems.
sources.source_geographic_coverage: Near-global land excluding Antarctica; source quality is lower north of 60 degrees north
sources.source_native_resolution: River reaches extracted from HydroSHEDS 15 arc-second hydrography with 10 km2 upstream-area or 0.1 m3/s discharge initiation
sources.source_variable_units: dimensionless exponent from log main-channel length versus log upstream area
sources.source_processing: Stream global DBF; select NEXT_DOWN = 0, ENDORHEIC = 0, ORD_CLAS = 1, and UPLAND_SKM >= 1000000; ordinary least-squares fit of log(DIST_UP_KM) on log(UPLAND_SKM)

sources.tolerance_basis: Physical-floor interval from zero to the HydroRIVERS natural-log RMSE plus 0.25, allowing coarse generated ocean-outlet watershed backbones more multiplicative scatter while retaining a bounded comparison; not a statistical confidence interval.
